name: gap_fill_fade_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Small gaps (0.3%-1.5%) in liquid stocks tend to fill within the session because they reflect overnight noise (global cues, ADR pricing) rather than genuine information. Market makers and institutional rebalancers push price back toward the prior close. The inefficiency persists because retail traders often interpret gaps as directional signals and chase them, providing the counterparty flow for gap-fill traders. Larger gaps (>2%) are excluded as they more likely reflect genuine information (earnings, events).
stock_filter: top 50 by 20-day avg turnover in FnO

indicators.name: gap_direction
indicators.purpose: 1 for gap up, -1 for gap down

long.confirmation: first green bar (close > open) after gap down, within first 20 bars

short.confirmation: first red bar (close < open) after gap up, within first 20 bars

exit.stop_loss: 0.5% beyond the gap extreme (for gap down long: 0.5% below session low)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 50% gap fill
exit.time_stop: exit after 120 bars if gap not filled
exit.signal_exit: exit if price extends gap by another 0.3% beyond entry

filters.time_filter: entry only in first 30 bars of session
filters.volume_filter: opening 5-min volume must be > average opening 5-min volume
filters.trend_filter: skip if gap direction aligns with 5-day trend (gap is trend continuation)
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for that stock, skip on RBI/budget days
other_filters: skip if gap > 1.5% (likely information-driven, not noise)
skip if gap < 0.3% (not enough edge to cover costs)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, gap fill tendency is robust across markets

weaknesses: Not all gaps fill. Information-driven gaps (earnings, sector rotation, policy shock) can persist. The 1.5% cap helps but doesn't eliminate this risk.
Opening 10 minutes have extreme slippage and wide spreads — actual fill quality is worse than backtest assumes. The 4 bps slippage may still be optimistic.
On days with broad market gaps (NIFTY gaps 1%+), correlated gap fills across multiple names create concentrated risk.
prior_art: Gap fill / gap fade is a well-documented anomaly. See: Quantifiable Edges blog, Connors Research. Edge is in the gap size filter and timing.
notes: Track gap fill rates by gap size bucket (0.3-0.5%, 0.5-1%, 1-1.5%) monthly. Kill the strategy if fill rate drops below 55% in any bucket.
